title: Nineteen Drawings and One Missing Figure
subtitle: 测量与维度 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 测量与维度（科学与技术·测量与维度）
meta: 主题语境：测量与维度（科学与技术·测量与维度）　|　核心词汇：dimension　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dimension 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the surveyor ① took a dimension that no builder in the town would have trusted, and he said the taking was the whole of the drawing. The ② dimension, meaning the measurement and not the aspect, ran nineteen drawings and stayed unwritten on the sheet; a dimension, he said, is the only thing on a plan that is judged by how long it is left unfigured.

Every ③ dimension in that set had the same missing figure beside it, and the ④ dimension at the end, meaning the one they kept for the stair and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A dimension, his assistant said, is nine parts checking and one part somebody willing to take; the surveyor said the checking is the part that fills nineteen drawings.

The architect meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the dimension was the whole of the argument, meaning the aspect and not the measurement. The ⑥ dimension, meaning the aspect and not any of that, is the only thing in an argument that everybody raises and nobody measures; dimension, she said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a measurement and an aspect. She said the aspect is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ dimension had become a line in a schedule, and the schedule had become an argument about the missing figure. The ⑧ dimension of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in May, was one set and nineteen drawings of checking; dimension, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to check. She said the checking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dimension I remember is the one at the end, which was confirmed in 1973 and is still described as the strangest in the set. A ⑩ dimension, the assistant said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being checked; every dimension, she said, is an aspect that has agreed to look like a measurement. She said the aspect was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 尺寸；尺度（指图纸上量得的那一处）
B. n. 尺寸（指那个量值本身，与那个方面相对）
C. 固定搭配：take a dimension 量取一个尺寸
D. n. 尺寸（指留给楼梯用的那一处）
E. n. 尺寸；量度（抽象总称，指一套图纸的全部标注）
F. n. 尺寸（指明细表上写到、被列出的那一处）
G. n. 方面；维度（指争论中被提出的那个层面）
H. n. 层面（抽象总称，指人人提出却无人衡量的那个）

items.q: took a dimension that no builder in the town would have trusted
The dimension, meaning the measurement and not the aspect
the dimension was the whole of the argument

The dimension of the whole thing

answers.why: take a dimension 意为“量取一个尺寸”，1951 年测量员量取了一个全镇没有一位建造商肯相信的尺寸。
dimension 意为“尺寸”，指那个量值本身而不是那个方面，它历经十九张图纸而在图页上没有数字。
dimension 意为“尺寸、尺度”，指那套图纸里每一处尺寸，每一处旁边都缺着同一个数字。
dimension 意为“尺寸”，指留给楼梯用的那一处，是唯一有人核对过两次的。
dimension 意为“方面、维度”，指争论中被提出的那个层面，建筑师说这个层面就是那场争论的全部。
dimension 意为“层面”，指人人提出却无人衡量的那个而不是那个量值，是争论里人人都提出、却无人去衡量的东西。
dimension 意为“尺寸”，指明细表上写到、被列出的那一处，到 1959 年这处尺寸成了明细表里的一行。
dimension 意为“尺寸、量度”，测量员五月写道，整件事的标注是一套图纸和十九张的核对。
dimension 意为“尺寸”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1973 年被确认，至今仍被说成全套里最奇的一处。
dimension 为抽象总称，助手 1975 年说，一处尺寸是唯一会因为被核对而变得更好的东西。
